text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created 2445009999 - streaming mux experiencing severe backlog; streaming frame delivery lagging, non-stream gen endpoints still healthy. Paging primary @sarah.k and infra @mike.r.

sarah.k: Looking at the streaming mux dashboard - sudden jump in queued tokens and long tail latencies for SSE clients. Can someone pull recent p95/p99 and active connection counts? link: https://metrics.redwood.example/d/streaming-mux

mike.r: pulling now. p95 token latency up from ~150ms to ~420ms over 10m, p99 from 700ms -> 1.8s. Active SSE connections doubled on a couple shards. Scheduling backlog shows many pending decode tasks. Correlation: deploy of mux-proxy v2.12 ~35m ago.

sarah.k: Customer impact? Which routes are hot and any enterprise routes hitting it? @jordan can you enumerate active enterprise SSE sessions?

jordan: ~900 SSE sessions total, ~55 enterprise-labeled routes, top 5 customers (C-209, C-344, C-778, C-901, C-605) generate ~70% of streaming tokens in last 30m. Most are on shared (hosted) pools. Not on Dedicated. Also noticed an increase in multi-thousand token contexts.

sarah.k: Mitigation brainstorm: A) per-connection token throttling, B) limit max simultaneous SSE frames, C) flip streaming to buffered responses for affected shards, D) shift heavy routes to non-streaming API with 429 guidance. Fastest reversible is likely toggling buffered mode. Thoughts?

eva: I recommend option C - set MUX_PUSH_MODE=buffered on targeted shards. That reduces SSE connection overhead and avoids partial frame churn. We can do a staged rollout by shard. I'll prepare the opsctl command.

mike.r: Confirmed. The mux honors MUX_PUSH_MODE environment flag; setting to "buffered" makes proxy buffer until completion and return a single response. No model restarts required. Canary is safe.

sarah.k: Ok, do a 10% shard canary first, watch queue depth/p99 for 5m, then expand. Also add a temporary per-connection token cap STREAM_SESSION_LIMIT=1200 for non-enterprise so single hogs can't starve others.

eva: rollout steps:
```
# set buffered mode for route-group heavy-streams
opsctl env-set --service mux-proxy --env MUX_PUSH_MODE=buffered --selector route-group=heavy-streams --ttl 45m --reason "emergency buffered mode to reduce SSE churn"
# add token cap
opsctl config-set --name STREAM_SESSION_LIMIT --value 1200 --scope default --ttl 45m
# monitor metrics for 5-10m
```
Kicking canary now.

eva: canary started at 2445010010. Monitoring: canary shard queue depth dropping, p99 on canary shard ~650ms down from 1.8s. No spike in 5xx.

mike.r: Good signal. GPU scheduling backlog improved on canary. Throughput tokens/sec increased ~20% on that shard.

sarah.k: Move to 40% after 3 minutes if stable. Jordan prep customer note template for enterprise contacts. Pager duty note to be updated.

eva: expanding to 40% at 2445010115.

ops-alert: :white_check_mark: 40% rollout success. No new 5xx, p99 for affected pool ~500-700ms. Queue overall trending down.

jordan: customer teaser note ready:
- impact: streaming will be delivered as a single buffered response for affected shards for ~45m; SSE interactive updates paused.
- rationale: reduce high per-connection overhead causing latency for many clients.
- workaround: use non-streaming generate endpoint; behavior unchanged.
- ETA: will update within 45m.

sarah.k: Good. Mike - can you scan recent commits on mux-proxy for anything that could increase KV churn or session invalidations? Tag PRs/authors.

mike.r: Found a change in session affinity logic from PR #4987 (author @nate) that adjusted cookie rotation frequency - this may increase KV invalidations for long-running sessions. I'll prepare a revert PR. If revert safe, we can plan to roll back once buffered-mode stabilizes.

sarah.k: What's fallback plan if buffered mode causes issues?

mike.r: Revert PR quickly (hotfix) or alternately re-enable streaming and enforce per-connection throttles (STREAM_RATE_LIMIT=100tokens/s) to protect scheduler.

eva: We'll hold buffered-mode and token cap for 45m. I'll also deploy a temporary metric for KV invalidation rate so we can quantify the root cause.

pagerduty-bot: @sarah.k acknowledged incident. Handoff reminder in 30m.

eva: added KV invalidation metric at 2445010280. Initial numbers show a spike aligning with PR deploy.

mike.r: Working on PR #4999 revert. Will bench test and if passes, ship to canary control plane.

sarah.k: Jordan, send the enterprise note now. Post a status update to status.redwood.example and #status-updates.

jordan: Sent email + status page update: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2445009999

sarah.k: Current impact metrics: global queue from ~2200 -> ~480 in 25m, p99 global down to ~520ms, error rate steady. This mitigation looks effective.

eva: Also set a short-lived circuit to limit new SSE setup rate: SSE_ACCEPT_RATE=200/min for default pool to reduce connection flapping.

mike.r: Revert PR prepared and smoke-tested on staging. If we push the revert, we'll schedule a small streaming canary after revert to validate lower KV invalidations.

sarah.k: Plan: keep buffered-mode + token cap for 45m, deploy revert to staging and QA, then stage rollback to streaming with phased canary. If regress, keep buffered-mode until we ship a deeper fix. Postmortem required.

oncall-shadow: I'll take handoff if incident persists past my shift start. Leaving notes in the ticket for continuity.

eva: 2445010240 - buffering flags still holding and metrics stable. Leaving TTL at 45m to avoid churn.

sarah.k: Incident status: MITIGATED - streaming temporarily buffered; monitoring ongoing. Owner: sarah.k. Follow-ups: revert session-affinity change, add streaming stress tests in CI, add alert for KV invalidation spikes. Postmortem sync tomorrow.

oncall-bot: Incident 2445009999 updated: MITIGATED. Incident remains open until rollback verification.

mike.r: Filed TODOs in the incident ticket: e2e streaming load test, refine session affinity behavior, add KV invalidation alert, document emergency flag ops.

eva: I'll prepare a short ops-runbook snippet for buffered-mode toggles so oncall can act faster next time.

sarah.k: Final note 2445010250 - queue and latencies stable. Keeping mitigations until revert is validated. Thanks all. :heart:
